ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the ratio of the measures of $\angle AOC$ to $\angle BOC$ is $5\colon 2$. $OD$ bisects $\angle AOB$. If $\angle COD=15^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle AOB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the ratio of the measures of $\angle AOC$ to $\angle BOC$ is $5\colon 2$,\\
let $\angle AOC=5x$ and $\angle BOC=2x$, then $\angle AOB=7x$,\\
since OD bisects $\angle AOB$,\\
it follows that $\angle BOD= \frac{1}{2} \angle AOB= \frac{7}{2} x$,\\
since $\angle COD=\angle BOD-\angle BOC$ and $\angle COD=15^\circ$,\\
then $\frac{7}{2} x-2x=15^\circ$,\\
solving for $x$ gives $x=10^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle AOB=7\times 10^\circ=\boxed{70^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the ratio of the measures of $\angle AOC$ to $\angle BOC$ is $5\colon 2$. $OD$ bisects $\angle AOB$. If $\angle COD=15^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle AOB$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the ratio of the measures of $\angle AOC$ to $\angle BOC$ is $5\colon 2$,\\
let $\angle AOC=5x$ and $\angle BOC=2x$, then $\angle AOB=7x$,\\
since OD bisects $\angle AOB$,\\
it follows that $\angle BOD= \frac{1}{2} \angle AOB= \frac{7}{2} x$,\\
since $\angle COD=\angle BOD-\angle BOC$ and $\angle COD=15^\circ$,\\
then $\frac{7}{2} x-2x=15^\circ$,\\
solving for $x$ gives $x=10^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle AOB=7\times 10^\circ=\boxed{70^\circ}$

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: All rays in the figure emanate from point O; in order from top to bottom they are OA, OD, OC, OB. Therefore C is inside ∠AOB, D is between OA and OC, and OD is located above OC. Reasoning: It is known that the ratio of the measures of ∠AOC and ∠BOC is 5:2. Let ∠AOC=5x and ∠BOC=2x. Because C is inside ∠AOB, ∠AOB=∠AOC+∠BOC=7x. Also because OD bisects ∠AOB, ∠BOD=1/2∠AOB=7x/2. From the order in the figure, ∠COD=∠BOD-∠BOC, therefore 7x/2-2x=15. Simplifying gives 3x/2=15, so x=10. Thus ∠AOB=7x=70°.
